item.title: The upcoming stop-motion series will stream exclusively on Disney+ and DisneyXD, as revealed in a special showcase during PokémonXP.
item.description: The upcoming stop-motion series will stream exclusively on Disney+ and DisneyXD, as revealed in a special showcase during PokémonXP. PokémonXP is underway, marking the debut of the very first fan convention completely dedicated to all-things Pokémon. Of course, some exclusive reveals and big announcements are expected, and one of those involves the brand’s next big animated series. First announced in July 2025, The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d and Pichu is exactly what it sounds like — a charming, humorous romp that follows the two Pokémon as they get into all sorts of hijinks in Galar. As revealed at PokémonXP, the series will be streamed exclusively on Disney+ and the DisneyXD channel. This was an unexpected turn of events, as the brand’s first stop motion series, Pokémon Concierge, streams solely on Netflix.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature at least one character from GTA Online.
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature at least one character from GTA Online. In Rockstar's extended look at GTA 6, fans were introduced to a bunch of characters with a wide range of morals. One character that fans probably overlooked is Valentina, a woman who was introduced last year in GTA Online. She makes her debut in a cutscene for the Money Fronts update, where she can be seen hopping off a private jet and interacting with Mr. Faber. While her role didn't seem especially significant at the time, it looks like she'll have a larger part to play in GTA 6. The character hires Jason and Lucia to be security for a VIP who is attending a party that is inevitably disrupted by gun-wielding goons. It's unclear if Valentina will have a larger role in GTA 6 outside of this mission, but it wouldn't be surprising if she did. It also raises the question of what else, or who else, Rockstar has been planting in GTA Online all these years. Of course, fans are hopeful to see Michael, Franklin, and Trevor return in GTA 6, but it remains to be seen if that will actually happen. Valentina is the first GTA Online character confirmed to return in GTA 6.#GTAVI pic.twitter.com/CbzzQAudDF

item.title: Callina Liang, who plays Chun-Li in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie, revealed the protein-heavy diet and intense workout routine she followed to bring the First Lady of Fighting Games to life.
item.description: Callina Liang, who plays Chun-Li in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie, revealed the protein-heavy diet and intense workout routine she followed to bring the First Lady of Fighting Games to life. If there’s one thing Chun-Li is known for — besides being the Strongest Woman in the World, of course — it’s her thick, muscular thunder thighs, which have only gotten more impressive with each new Street Fighter game. From Third Strike to Street Fighter V and now Street Fighter 6, it’s clear the devs at Capcom have a clear vision in mind for the character’s physical appearance. (And we thank them for it.) Callina Liang knew this was an important thing to get right, so she buckled down and began following a strict martial arts workout routine and eating a high-protein diet to help grow her muscles — to the point where she almost got sick. "Chun-Li is all kicks. So we did a bunch of Taekwondo training, Muay Thai, and Wushu (Kung Fu). I did two hours of that a day and strengthened my legs a lot and changed my diet drastically. When I was bulking, I ate 12 eggs a day. Every two hours I had to have a meal, and I was on the verge of throwing up. But it worked. By the end of the shoot, my thighs had grown six-and-a-half centimeters each,” she said in an August interview with Empire Magazine.

item.title: Capcom is making thirsty fans’ dreams come true for Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary exhibition, revealing that it will display life-sized statues of Lady Dimitrescu and Albert Wesker.
item.description: Capcom is making thirsty fans’ dreams come true for Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary exhibition, revealing that it will display life-sized statues of Lady Dimitrescu and Albert Wesker. There’s something for everyone at Capcom’s RE anniversary extravaganza. Coming to the Shibuya BEAM Gallery from October 30 to December 24, the exhibition will feature real-life recreations of iconic items and creatures from the famous horror game franchise, including “life-sized models of villains crafted with meticulous detail,” as told by SaigaNAK. Two of these villains have been revealed, and the reactions from the internet have not disappointed. As posted on the exhibition's official website in late August, Resident Evil antagonist Albert Wesker and Village’s Lady Dimitrescu are getting life-sized statues at the Shibuya exhibition. Concept art for these sculptures have also been shared, showing Lady D sitting in an ornate, plush chair while Wesker stands tall, wearing his iconic sunglasses and trenchcoat combo.

item.title: The Xbox Series X25 anniversary console is officially up for pre-order, so you know what that means: scalpers are cashing in.
item.description: The Xbox Series X25 anniversary console is officially up for pre-order, so you know what that means: scalpers are cashing in. Like clockwork, pre-order pages for Microsoft's 25th anniversary console were bombarded by buyers when they went live yesterday, August 27, 2026. At $899.99 for that translucent green box and $79.99 for its themed controller, the price to celebrate Xbox's birthday was already quite steep, but scalpers have still seemingly managed to find buyers willing to spend thousands. In the 24 hours since pre-order pages went live, multiple listings have popped up on eBay and, in many cases, successfully sold the Xbox Series X25 console bundle for more than $2,000. One scalper selling the full package – which Microsoft said comes with the "XBOX 25" branded 1TB console and controller, as well as a copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved – managed to successfully close a listing for $2,800. Many, many others have managed to sell their confirmed purchases for around $2,500. That's a remarkable increase for an already pricey Xbox console, but the individual controller is getting hit just as hard. If you want to pick up one of the controllers (which also happen to have the original Xbox logo hidden in the back) from eBay, you could be spending as much as $185, more than double its retail cost. Many others are going for around $130.

Nvidia debuted DLSS 5 back in March 2026, promising to bring neural rendering to games in order to make them look more realistic. While pretty much everyone hated it, it seems like Nvidia has continued to work on it behind the scenes: It's leaked in a build of the NBA 2K27 beta. Twitter user @renan_maniero spotted the new DLSS file in the NBA 2K27 early access, called nvngx_dlssnr.dll. The 'nr' at the end there appears to stand for neural rendering. Just finding the file in the game's directory would be one thing, but it looks like some enterprising modders have been able to build it into some other existing games. Eita, o acesso antecipado do jogo NBA 2K27 veio com uma DLL nova do DLSS. DLSS-NR (Neural Rendering) 👀 pic.twitter.com/X15fYO92RU Some modders built a DLSS 5 mod and integrated it into Control, which was spotted by Gizmodo. In the initial post on X, you can see the modders manipulating some sliders to change the degree by which the neural renderer is changing the image. Things like auto skin mask, intensity and style are all customizable, which is something Nvidia said would be possible when it announced the technology earlier this year.

item.title: Getting Rockstar's hugely ambitious GTA 6 running at 60fps on current consoles will be "extremely unlikely", the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said, after analysis of footage from the Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look.
item.description: Getting Rockstar's hugely ambitious GTA 6 running at 60fps on current consoles will be "extremely unlikely", the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said, after analysis of footage from the Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look. Yesterday's 27-minute reveal featured 30fps footage of the game on Netflix, YouTube, and in the raw file made available by Rockstar to download — and this is seemingly how we should all expect the game to look when it arrives on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S this November. While 30fps might seem low compared to the frame counts of other modern gaming blockbusters, Rockstar appears to be targeting this level to maximize the sheer detail on offer in every one of those frames, Digital Foundry believes. "It's clear that the focus was absolutely maximising the level of visual detail at a fixed 30fps frame-rate on all platforms," Digital Foundry wrote in an Extended Look deep dive article. "The rendering, simulation and presentation have all been tuned around that constraint - and the result is an unprecedented level of density, material quality and world coherence, with trade-offs landing primarily in image quality and animation smoothness rather than systemic scale or fidelity."

item.title: Hawkeye star Jeremy Renner appears to be teasing a long-awaited return to the MCU, as a final round of Avengers: Doomsday reshoots reportedly gets underway.
item.description: Hawkeye star Jeremy Renner appears to be teasing a long-awaited return to the MCU, as a final round of Avengers: Doomsday reshoots reportedly gets underway. Renner posted what appeared to be a clear tease for his involvement via Instagram today, with a photo of his Hawkeye costume set to the "Hawkeye Theme" music. The timing of this post is very interesting, as it follows confirmation this week from M'Baku actor Winston Duke, who stated that "additional photography for Avengers: Doomsday" is now underway, per an interview with CNA. Of course, Avengers: Doomsday is now just four months from launch — meaning that any additional material shot now has a just limited time to be worked into the production. But Marvel seems to have planned for this situation, with filming essentially tacked on to the start of filming for 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars, which is expected to begin its own production shoot in September.

item.title: Did you spot the world of Red Dead Redemption 2 in last night's GTA 6 Extended Look? Rockstar's cowboy epic made a brief appearance — and, of course, some fans spotted it immediately.
item.description: Did you spot the world of Red Dead Redemption 2 in last night's Grand Theft Auto 6 Extended Look? Rockstar's cowboy epic made a brief appearance — and, of course, some GTA 6 fans spotted it immediately. During a TV commercial for what might be the unhealthiest burger ever invented, a lush outdoor scene features in the background. A winding river courses through green trees, with several notable rock formations on its banks. Adorning the scene are an array of animals — which will presumably soon be turned into the burger's 30,000 calorie contents. Even more excitingly for Rockstar's fans, however, this was clearly footage taken within Red Dead Redemption 2, and players rushed to reach the exact spot. There's no array of animals here normally, and clearly Rockstar has made a couple of tweaks with its lighting. But the river is the same, as are the trees and most of the rocks. It's a fun Easter egg for fans of the developer's previous game, now looking forward to its next. If you want to visit it yourself, reddit user DangerousLeo (who found the exact spot) has highlighted the U-bend in the Kamassa River, north-west of Annesburg, just to the west of Deer Cottage. (How did DangerousLeo find the location so quickly? Well, they admit to having more than 730 hours logged on Red Dead Redemption 2 to date.)

item.title: Netflix US viewership spiked by 50% yesterday as Rockstar debuted its Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look.
item.description: Netflix US viewership spiked by 50% yesterday as Rockstar debuted its Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look. That's according to audience data provided to IGN by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, when comparing Netflix's US audience to the same time on the previous day. Compared to the streamer's average US viewership over the past 12 weeks on a Thursday, mobile use was up almost 50%. Web visitors soared by 125%, meanwhile, as countless subscribers tuned in from their PCs (perhaps sneakily watching from work or classes). While the launch of Netflix's GTA 6 broadcast was ultimately successful, users in multiple countries reported experiencing momentary technical difficulties at the moment of its premiere. If you saw the below error screen — featuring someone's hand and a very wonky cake — you certainly were not alone. Countless users reported seeing similar across social media, including high-profile streamers, and we certainly saw the same here at IGN. Thankfully, the problem resolved itself within around 30 seconds.

item.title: Rockstar has discussed the need to "be careful" with its satirical take on American culture in GTA 6, when asked about including references to recent events such as the Covid pandemic and Donald Trump's presidency.
item.description: Rockstar has discussed the need to "be careful" with its satirical take on American culture in GTA 6, when asked about including references to recent events such as the Covid pandemic and Donald Trump's presidency. Speaking to French outlet Trois Couleurs, Rockstar Games head of development Rob Nelson cited the "very long" development cycle of GTA 6 as a reason why Rockstar was cautious about what it parodies — to ensure things "stand the test of time." "We develop on very long cycles," Nelson said. "The game's been in development since 2015, so the idea is gestating for a long time. The majority of the team really started rolling on to it after Red Dead Redemption 2 released in 2018. "We have to be very careful about what ideas we choose to put in there, because it can take a long time to figure out what our angle is on this," he added. "Because by the time we write it and cast it and shoot it, and implement it, whatever it is – it could be gone, it could change, it could be dated. And so we're always trying to think about whether something will stand the test of time."

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6's map is significantly larger than Rockstar's previous games; here's how it compares to the studio's other titles.
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6's map is significantly larger than the maps in Rockstar's previous games. Here's how it compares to the studio's other titles, according to the developer. Rockstar Games confirmed to The New York Times and YouTuber TGG that Grand Theft Auto 6's map is three times bigger than the playable area of Red Dead Redemption 2. Elaborating to TGG, it was revealed that it is twice the size of Grand Theft Auto 5, and Vice City itself is twice the size of Los Santos from GTA 5. Vice City and its surrounding suburbs are 11 times bigger than Los Santos and its surrounding areas. If that wasn't enough for you, TGG also revealed that there are "hundreds" of accessible interiors in GTA 6. In GTA 5, players could enter the homes of their respective characters, different shops, and a few random buildings like the Los Santos police station, but generally speaking, there weren't a lot of places you could enter. GTA Online has added more over time, but they often require loading screens and are very restrictive. The GTA 6 extended look already showed off a variety of interiors both inside and outside of missions, so that should make Leonida a lot more layered. Speaking to IGN, Rockstar Games' Rob Nelson discussed how the developer took lessons learned from building Red Dead Redemption 2's version of the Wild West and expanded upon those ideas with GTA 6.

item.title: The official Pokémon profile on X has responded after its account was hacked by an unknown party who shared a post linking out to a memecoin.
item.description: The official Pokémon profile on X has responded after its account was hacked by an unknown party who shared a post linking out to a memecoin. The hack occurred around 3pm PT on August 17, 2026. The post — which has since been deleted — was cleverly structured, appearing as an official Pokémon advertisement with a link to a site that, at first glance, looked like a legitimate page celebrating the brand’s 30th anniversary, which is ongoing. “Celebrate 30 years of Pokémon in a whole new way!” the post read. “Introducing $POKEMON, the official Pokemon memecoin. Join trainers around the world and be part of the #Pokemon30 celebration.” The post was up for around 30 minutes before it was finally taken down. Most commenters weren’t fooled, though, and it wasn’t long before proposed community notes began appearing underneath the supposed scam on X.

item.title: Rockstar Games has finally revealed an official look at GTA 6 gameplay, and members of the development team couldn't be happier to finally see fans' reactions.
item.description: Rockstar Games has finally revealed an official look at Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay, and members of the development team couldn't be happier to finally see fans' reactions. Our first real glimpse at what the GTA 6 studio has been cooking up finally arrived as part of the Netflix extended look today. While there's still plenty of side activities, romance subplots, and robberies for Jason and Lucia that we've yet to see, the developers at Rockstar are just happy their work can be shown off as intended. "Our Teams across the World have worked incredibly hard," production designer Terrance Radcliff said. "So proud of everyone. Watching this with coworkers as a Family – and when I get home I’ll watch again with my Family!" "The first ever game I have played was Vice City as a kid," graphic programmer Mert Kirimgeri said. "It's an honour to be working with the most professional, brilliant and kind people on the planet over the most immersive game ever made, not to mention one of the most complex computer systems in human existence. Enjoy!!!"

item.title: Star Citizen single-player spinoff Squadron 42 has been delayed to 2027, with developer Chris Roberts insisting it wouldn't get the attention it deserves because of Grand Theft Auto 6.
item.description: Star Citizen single-player spinoff Squadron 42 has been delayed to 2027, with developer Chris Roberts insisting it wouldn't get the attention it deserves because of Grand Theft Auto 6. In a new blog post, Cloud Imperium Games CEO Chris Roberts announced that Squadron 42 will be launching in Q2 2027. The studio had previously announced 2026 as its release window and reaffirmed late last year that it was still targeting that. However, Roberts noted that GTA 6 is going to suck up all of the attention this fall, and as a result, it doesn't make sense to launch a new game during that time. "At CitizenCon 2024, we announced we would ship in 2026. Our plan was to release in Q4 around IAE," said Roberts. "But much like the rest of the industry there is no way I want to launch my spiritual successor to Wing Commander, a game that has had twelve years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it (we started Squadron 42 development in 2014 as 2013 was opening studios, hiring people and getting the Hangar module out for Star Citizen) launching into the attention buzz saw of GTA 6. While GTA 6 isn’t launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage." Roberts went on to note that CIG will be doing previews of Squadron 42 with content creators and early backers in October, which it will use as an opportunity to announce release plans with a concrete date to follow "shortly" afterwards. Q2 would place Squadron 42 sometime during the spring, so long as nothing changes between now and then.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 will take a while for players to finish, with the game's producer stating it took him 80 hours.
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 will take a while for players to finish, with the game's producer stating it took him 80 hours. In an The New York Times interview, Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson revealed that it took him about 80 hours to finish the game in February. He noted that included the main story and some "optional goals with narrative ramifications," it's unclear if that included just mucking about in the open world or anything, though. Still, that is a sizable length regardless. Nelson ultimately hopes fans take their time with the game and don't rush through it. For comparison, GTA 4 and 5 are around 30 hours long, while Red Dead Redemption 2 is around 50-60 hours. So, that means GTA 6 will be the longest of Rockstar's games to date, which will be reassuring for fans who have waited a long time for this game. Assuming 80 hours doesn't include the time for 100% completion, there will still be plenty of ways to extend your time with the game. Grand Theft Auto 6 has no shortage of open-world activities, including basketball, fishing, exercising, and much more. There will also likely be a plethora of side missions for players to indulge in, so it seems like we'll all be playing GTA 6 for a long time. Red Dead Redemption 2 has kept players very active thanks to its level of depth and detail, thanks to unique NPCs, hidden details, and side content.
